run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout since 2026-11-16T12:30:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/checkout matches checkout's own telemetry: the only checkout span groups carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR are the PlaceOrder server span (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) and its HTTP server span, and the 2-minute error share rose from 0 at 12:30 to roughly 20-45% from 12:34 onward (with a dip to ~1.3-2.9% at 12:58-12:59), which is consistent with the 0.2 value in the alert annotation. Every sampled PlaceOrder error carries the exact text 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'. The failing span chain in every inspected failing trace is prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart -> an error-marked checkout 'HTTP POST' whose only child is the shipping service's '/get-quote' server span (31-469 microseconds), with no 'POST quote' child and no per-item ProductCatalog/Currency call spans; successful PlaceOrder traces, by contrast, contain per-item GetProduct/Convert spans, a shipping '/get-quote' that calls quote, and a checkout POST to email that returns 200. So checkout's order fails when it posts an empty shipping-quote request to shipping and receives HTTP 400, and checkout turns that into gRPC INTERNAL. The message text names the email service, but email's own telemetry contradicts that reading: email only ever produced POST /send_order_confirmation spans with no error status, one per successful order, and no email span appears in any failing trace. Email, payment and accounting show no failure of their own; all 21 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts. What remains unresolved is which object is defective: whether shipping's rejection of an empty quote request is intended, and why the cart read at checkout returns no items. Both candidates are reported as hypotheses; valkey-cart running at a 10Mi memory limit (working set 10,010,624 bytes at 13:05) is noted as an unverified risk.

claims.text: In service checkout the only span groups with STATUS_CODE_ERROR are span_name 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and span_name 'HTTP POST'; checkout's client spans to CartService/GetCart, CartService/EmptyCart, PaymentService/Charge, CurrencyService/Convert and ProductCatalogService/GetProduct are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so no downstream client span of checkout carries an error status.

Checkout PlaceOrder error counts per 2-minute increase were 0 at the evaluation ending 12:30, 4 (12:31), 10.67 (12:33), 24 (12:34) and 48 (12:35) against 64-68 non-error spans, i.e. an error share around 20-45% from 12:34 through 12:56; the share collapsed to 1.33 errors/69.33 and 2.91/94.6 at 12:58-12:59 and re-ramped to 30.67 errors/73.33 by 13:08.

Every sampled failing PlaceOrder span carries otel.status_description and exception.message 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400' with otel.status_code ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code 13; the frontend's client span in the same trace shows grpc.error_message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'.

In failing trace d874ecb25904ac342b44dc2531ee269f the checkout span prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart has exactly two children: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (219.8 ms, rpc.grpc.status_code 0) and a checkout 'HTTP POST' span marked error whose only child is the shipping service span '/get-quote' lasting 31 microseconds; that trace contains no ProductCatalog or Currency spans from checkout and no 'POST quote' span from shipping.

The second failing trace fabf30c40bb674e79e93dd78836bb231 shows the same shape: prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart (22.0 ms) has only GetCart (20.9 ms, rpc.grpc.status_code 0) and an error-marked checkout 'HTTP POST' (826 microseconds) whose only child is shipping '/get-quote' (469 microseconds), again with no 'POST quote' child and no per-item ProductCatalog/Currency spans.

Successful PlaceOrder traces (rpc.grpc.status_code 0, e.g. ca1b7768dded1c3767355f45a235bd41 and 25114e0061bd26ddb5976a21d1ab8207) do contain per-item checkout spans oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert, and shipping '/get-quote' lasts 1.96-36.4 ms with a child 'POST quote' whose child is quote 'POST /getquote'.

In successful traces the email call is checkout 'HTTP POST' -> email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' with http.status_code 200 (e.g. 4.4 ms and 4.5 ms spans), and email's only observed operations are 'POST /send_order_confirmation' (server), 'send_email' and 'sinatra.render_template', none ever recorded with an error status.

Email request volume tracks successful checkouts, not all checkouts: in the 30-minute bucket ending 13:05 email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' counted 1498.98 spans while checkout PlaceOrder counted 1498 UNSET and 722 ERROR spans, and all email series carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for email).

In the shipping pod logs the failing request served at 12:34:45.586 has no corresponding worker log line: the nearest entries are a 'Requesting quote'/'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' triple at 12:34:45.353 and another triple at 12:34:45.889, whereas normal quote traffic shows continuous paired 'Requesting quote' and 'Sending Quote' lines through 12:34:50-13:04.

Checkout's container configuration sets SHIPPING_ADDR=http://shipping:8080 and EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080; the shipping container has QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 and no email address; the email container has EMAIL_PORT=8080. Service endpoints resolve email->email-59f69bc6cf-7wqqk, shipping->shipping-75d58f5d84-kgmz9 and quote->quote-6b5877698d-x6v2f, and the email, shipping and quote deployments each report 1/1 available replicas.

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState recorded for any container; every application pod was created around 12:19:57, while the load-generator pod load-generator-7d5756fbd9-zzj4z was created later, at 12:54:12.

The frontend service carries its own error spans for these same requests: 'POST /api/checkout' with http.status_code 500, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' with 500, and its client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and grpc.error_message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'.

Frontend-proxy error volume is far larger than the checkout failures and is not explained by them: span 'ingress' with STATUS_CODE_ERROR counted 41,125 per 30 minutes in the bucket ending 13:05 versus 722 ERROR PlaceOrder spans, and the sampled failing trace contains an ingress span of 15.0 s with http.status_code 504 while the frontend POST in the same trace returned 200 after 97 ms.

Cart request volume was sustained, not collapsing: in 5-minute increases the cart service handled AddItem 820-1115, GetCart 1536.7-1932.2 and EmptyCart 203.8-290 spans, and EmptyCart volume is of the same order as successful PlaceOrder volume.

The valkey-cart container is limited to cpu 10m and memory 10Mi (cart itself to 45m/165Mi); valkey-cart memory working set grew from 7,733,248 bytes at 12:30 to 10,010,624 bytes at 13:05, i.e. to the edge of its 10Mi limit. CFS throttling ratios over 12:30-13:05 were 0.043-0.068 for valkey-cart and 0.180-0.253 for cart, and cart HGET p90 stayed at about 2 ms (2.86 ms at the 13:05 bucket).

The flagd configuration currently loaded in ConfigMap flagd-config sets every failure flag (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) to 'off' and defines no email- or shipping-failure flag, while loadGeneratorFloodHomepage has defaultVariant '100'.

Supported hypothesis for the alert: checkout's PlaceOrder fails because its outbound POST of the shipping quote to the shipping service's /get-quote endpoint is answered with HTTP 400 (checkout's own error text says 'got 400', and the error-marked checkout client span has the shipping /get-quote server span as its only child), and checkout converts that into gRPC INTERNAL for the whole PlaceOrder. In the failing requests checkout had no cart items to price (no ProductCatalog/Currency child spans) and shipping answered within 31-469 microseconds without calling quote and without writing a quote-request log line, which fits shipping rejecting an empty/invalid quote request.

Unresolved sub-cause: the sampled failing checkouts read an empty cart from the cart service (GetCart returns rpc.grpc.status_code 0 while no per-item lookups follow), so the empty quote request may originate in cart contents rather than in shipping. The cart's HGET tail latencies in those same failing traces (19.1 ms, 45.6 ms, 100.3 ms) are consistent with valkey-cart exhausting its 10m CPU quota per 100 ms CFS period, but no cart-side error, timeout or data-loss signal was observed, so this link is unverified.

The error message's reference to the email service conflicts with the routing evidence and remains unexplained: the failing outbound POST demonstrably reached the shipping service, checkout's EMAIL_ADDR and SHIPPING_ADDR point at different services (http://email:8080 and http://shipping:8080), and no email span appears in any failing trace. Reading the text literally would make the email service the failing dependency, which the email telemetry does not support, so the mismatch is a code/message-label question rather than an observed email failure.

Temporal correlation only, not causation: the failure share fell to 1.33/69.33 and 2.91/94.6 error/non-error spans at 12:58-12:59, a few minutes after the load-generator pod load-generator-7d5756fbd9-zzj4z was created at 12:54:12, and then re-ramped. This could reflect load-generator user/cart state being reset rather than any change in checkout, cart, shipping or email, none of which restarted.

The email service is not shown to be returning HTTP 400: its only operations are 'POST /send_order_confirmation', 'send_email' and 'sinatra.render_template', it produced no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, its request count matches successful checkouts (1498.98 vs 1498 UNSET PlaceOrder spans in the bucket ending 13:05), and no email span appears in the failing traces, where the request that failed went to shipping /get-quote.

Payment and accounting show zero ERROR spans over the 6-hour 30-minute-step view (0 for both at the 13:00 bucket), whereas checkout showed 1448.1 and frontend 2725.0, so the failure is not a general payment-path failure.

Rejected: that a pod crash, OOM kill or rescheduling of checkout, shipping, email or cart caused the errors. Every otel-demo pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState for any container, and checkout's own log stream for 12:34:52-12:34:55 shows the normal success sequence ('[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent to ...', 'sending to postProcessor') with no crash or restart signal.

Rejected as the cause of the alert: that the frontend-proxy or frontend is the origin. The frontend's error spans are the same request propagating checkout's gRPC INTERNAL (same trace, http.status_code 500 on 'POST /api/checkout'), and frontend-proxy error volume (41,125 ingress errors per 30 minutes) is two orders of magnitude larger than the 722 checkout PlaceOrder errors, so that volume is not attributable to this cause.

Confirm with the shipping service owner whether POST /get-quote is expected to answer HTTP 400 when the item list is empty, and decide whether checkout should treat an empty cart as an internal error (currently it surfaces as gRPC 13 INTERNAL and drives the alert) or handle it as a client-side condition.

Review the valkey-cart resource limits: its memory working set reached 10,010,624 bytes against a 10Mi limit at 13:05 and its CPU limit is 10m, with 4-7% of CFS periods throttled; the same review should establish whether short cart TTL or empty carts are expected from the load-generator's checkout flow.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule expression from Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration (it was not available in this target) and correct the misleading dependency name in checkout's error text, which says 'failed POST to email service' while the failing call went to the shipping service.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this Prometheus target (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate), so the alert's own expression, window and label filters could not be verified against the metric.

Only trace-derived span metrics exist for these services: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series, so the HTTP 400 that checkout reports could not be confirmed from a server-side HTTP status metric or from any email/shipping server request-status series.

Jaeger data ends around 12:34:54 in this target: traces_search for checkout in 12:40-13:05 and traces_search_by_tags for shipping '/get-quote' in 12:50-13:00 both returned no traces, so the failures observed in metrics from 12:35 to 13:09 were not trace-inspected; trace-based findings describe the 12:33-12:35 sample only.

The email pod produced no log lines at all for 12:25-13:05 (log view status no_data), and the cart and valkey-cart log queries returned no_data with no matching lines, so an absence of application errors in those containers is unknown rather than established.

A filtered search for checkout application error lines (12:25-13:05) returned no_data with 12,192 lines removed by the filter; this is not proof that checkout logged no error, only that the filtered view returned nothing citable.

Whether the shipping service's HTTP 400 is intended for an empty item list, and why the cart read at checkout returned no items, cannot be determined from the available sources; there is no change-history integration and no direct view of cart contents.

The flagd ConfigMap read is the cluster's current state, not its state during the incident, and these are application flags; any change to checkout/shipping/email configuration or cart state around 12:31 could not be verified.
frontend-proxy's very large ingress error volume (41,125 per 30 minutes) and the 15-second 504 observed alongside a 97 ms 200 response in one trace are unexplained and were not attributed.
next_steps: Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Prometheus/Alertmanager configuration and confirm which metric, labels and window it evaluates.
Ask the shipping and checkout owners whether an empty item list on POST /get-quote is a valid 400, and whether checkout is expected to call the quote endpoint for an empty cart.
Inspect cart key contents and TTL in valkey-cart (CART keys) and confirm whether carts are being emptied or expiring before checkout reads them.
Right-size valkey-cart (10Mi memory / 10m CPU) and cart (45m CPU) limits, given the valkey working set growth toward the memory limit and the observed CFS throttling.
Retain or extend trace retention so the 12:35-13:09 failure window can be inspected at the span level.
Check the load-generator's checkout task definition and the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage variant '100' to confirm whether checkouts are intentionally issued against empty carts.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows Prometheus's state at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window; it cannot show the state when the incident happened.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
